blocks.text: PHP is a server-side scripting language designed to be used for web purposes. Originally PHP was short for "Personal Home Page", but over time it evolved to include its recursive current expansion: "PHP: Hypertext Pre-processor".

blocks.caption: PHP — the server-side scripting language.

blocks.text: Server-side scripting languages interpret scripts on the server side rather than the client side (like JavaScript). Doing so provides a customised interface for each user and adds functionality beyond what HTML can offer. Scripting languages are programming languages that are interpreted rather than needing to be compiled before execution. Facebook, Wikipedia and WordPress are said to be using PHP.
Features of PHP

PHP allows interactive features not possible with HTML. In its earliest days it was used for hit counters and guest books; now developers use PHP to create web forms, forums, complex shopping carts and other features that encourage two-way interaction with visitors.

items: Open Source: PHP is an open-source scripting language, meaning its source code is freely available for anyone to view, modify and distribute.

Inexpensive Hosting and Setup: PHP is well supported by a wide range of web hosting providers, and hosting PHP-based websites tends to be more affordable than for other server-side scripting languages. PHP is also easy to set up.
Cross-Platform: PHP runs on various operating systems, including Linux, Windows, macOS and Unix-based systems, so it can be deployed on a wide range of servers without significant modification.

Client applications don't need PHP installed: unlike Python or Ruby, PHP is executed on the server side, so clients accessing PHP-driven web applications only need a web browser — they do not need PHP installed on their local machines.

Lots of free libraries and packages: PHP has a vast ecosystem of open-source libraries, frameworks and packages covering everything from database access and authentication to e-commerce and content management systems.

blocks.text: Overall, these benefits make PHP a popular choice for web development, particularly for creating dynamic and interactive websites and web applications. Its combination of versatility, accessibility and extensive community support has contributed to its widespread adoption.
Strengths of PHP

items: PHP is simple to learn and write. Anyone who knows HTML can quickly pick it up, and the two can be used interchangeably.
Since PHP is a dynamically typed language it is also highly flexible — there are no rules on how to build features, so developers have plenty of room for innovation.
Its flexibility goes beyond ease of use: PHP can handle a wide range of data types.
It integrates with all the popular databases, including MySQL, Postgres, Oracle and MS SQL Server.
PHP is well maintained and supported by a huge community, so it is likely to stay more current than other mature tools.
One side benefit of its popularity is that finding skilled developers is easy.
Programmer productivity stays high with PHP.
It operates at a request level with a full state reset for each request, so programmers have a more streamlined development experience; the structure makes debugging easier.

blocks.text: Weaknesses of PHP

items: PHP's main strength — flexibility — is also its weakness: it can be a little too forgiving of errors.
With no strict rules, inexperienced programmers have the freedom to create some very bad solutions to simple problems.
Bad packages that became popular in the community are still reused when developers are trying something new or are rushed for time; some of these mistakes lead to security risks.
Updates add features that clash with earlier features.
PHP is an interpreted language, which can reduce speed.
Scaling and maintaining PHP is a complicated endeavour.

blocks.text: PHP started out as a small open-source project that evolved as more and more people found out how useful it was. Rasmus Lerdorf unleashed the first version of PHP way back in 1994. PHP is one of the most widely used server-side scripting languages for web development; popular websites like Facebook, Yahoo and Wikipedia are developed using PHP. It is very simple to learn, code and deploy on a server, so it has been the first choice for beginners for decades.

A recursive acronym for "PHP: Hypertext Pre-processor". It is a server-side scripting language that is embedded in HTML and is used to manage dynamic content, databases and session tracking, and even to build entire e-commerce sites.

blocks.title: Key facts about PHP
items: It can be integrated with a number of popular databases, including MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, Sybase, Informix and Microsoft SQL Server.

PHP is dynamic in its execution, especially when compiled as an Apache module on the Unix side. The MySQL server, once started, executes even very complex queries with huge result sets in record-setting time.
PHP supports a large number of major protocols such as POP3, IMAP and LDAP.
PHP4 added support for Java and distributed object architectures (COM and CORBA), making n-tier development possible for the first time.
PHP is forgiving: the PHP language tries to be as forgiving as possible.
PHP syntax is similar to the C programming language.

blocks.text: Common Uses of PHP

items: PHP performs system functions — on files on a system it can create, open, read, write and close them.
PHP can handle forms — gather data from files, save data to a file, send data through email and return data to the user.
We add, delete and modify elements within the database through PHP.
It accesses cookies variables and sets cookies.
Using PHP we can restrict users from accessing some pages of a website.
It can encrypt data.

blocks.text: Characteristics of PHP
Five important characteristics make PHP's practical nature possible:

items: Simplicity.
Efficiency.
Security.
Flexibility.
Familiarity.

blocks.text: Software Requirements

blocks.title: To run PHP code we need the following software on the local machine:
items: Browser.
Web Server (e.g. Apache).
PHP (Interpreter).
MySQL Databases (this is optional).

blocks.text: We can install the Web Server, the PHP Interpreter and the MySQL databases separately. But to make the work easier, developers have produced all-in-one setup packages that automatically install and configure a PHP environment on Windows, Linux or Mac machines:

blocks.caption: All-in-one PHP packages
head: Package
Platform
Contents

blocks.text: The Process to Install PHP

blocks.title: Getting PHP running
items: To execute PHP code we need access to a web server on which PHP is running.
Install Apache and PHP, or install XAMPP, WAMP, LAMP or MAMP according to the operating system installed on the computer.
After installation, run and start the Apache server and PHP from the program list, then type http://localhost in the web browser to start working.
In the Apache installation folder you will find the www folder (in XAMPP it is htdocs), where you can save PHP files; you can also create your project folder inside it.
Alternatively, find a web hosting plan with Apache, PHP and MySQL support and run the PHP scripts on the web host.
You can also use an online interface such as runphponline.com to interpret PHP code online.

blocks.text: Hardware Requirements
The hardware requirements are not much — we just need a laptop or a desktop computer.

items: PHP 5.5+ requires a computer with at least Windows 2008/Vista, or 2008r2, 2012, 2012r2, 2016, or 7, 8, 8.1, 10 (both 32-bit and 64-bit). PHP does not run on Windows RT/WOA/ARM.
As of PHP 7.2.0, Windows 2008 and Vista are no longer supported.
A computer with a Pentium IV processor, 2 GB RAM, a 256 GB hard disk and a colour monitor or above is more than enough.

sections.title: Object Oriented Programming with Server-Side Scripting

blocks.text: Object-Oriented is an approach to software development that models applications around real-world objects such as employees, cars and bank accounts. A class defines the properties and methods of a real-world object. An object is an occurrence of a class. There are three major principles of OOP:

items: Encapsulation: concerned with hiding the implementation details and only exposing the methods. It is used to reduce software development complexity.
Inheritance: concerned with the relationship between classes. Its main purpose is re-usability.
Polymorphism: concerned with having a single form but many different implementation ways. Its main purpose is to simplify maintaining applications and make them more extendable.

blocks.text: PHP is an object-oriented programming language and supports all of the above principles. They are achieved via:

blocks.caption: How PHP implements the three OOP principles
head: Principle
Implemented in PHP by
rows: Using the same function or method name in many forms, i.e. with different numbers of parameters.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: OOP is treated in full in Chapter 5. This section is only a bridge: it tells you that the PHP you are about to learn can also be written in an object-oriented style.

PHP (Hypertext Pre-processor) is a widely used open-source general-purpose scripting language that can be embedded with HTML. PHP files are saved with the ".php" extension. PHP scripts can be written anywhere in the document, within PHP tags, alongside normal HTML.
PHP Tags — Escaping To PHP

The mechanism of separating normal HTML from PHP code. Various ways exist; a few methods are set by default, but to use others such as Short-open or ASP-style tags you must change the configuration of the php.ini file. These tags are also used for embedding PHP within HTML.
There are 4 such tags available:
1. Canonical PHP Tags
The script starts with <?php and ends with ?>. These are called 'Canonical PHP tags'. Every PHP command ends with a semi-colon (;).

<?php
   # Here echo command is used to print
   echo "Hello, world!";
?>

// Output
Hello, world!
2. SGML or Short HTML Tags
The shortest option to initialise PHP code: the script starts with <? and ends with ?>. It works only by setting the short_open_tag setting in the php.ini file to 'on'.

<?php
   # Here echo command will only work if
   # setting is done as said before
   echo "Hello, world!";
?>
3. HTML Script Tags
Implemented using script tags. This syntax was removed in PHP 7.0.0.

<?php
   echo "hello world!";
?>
4. ASP Style Tags
To use these you must configure the php.ini file. They are used by Active Server Pages to describe code blocks; they start with <% and end with %>.

<?php
   # Can only be written if setting is turned on
   # to allow %
   echo "hello world";
?>
Exam focus: always use the canonical <?php … ?> tag. It is the only one guaranteed to work on every server (MCQ 16 and 17 both test this).
Comments in PHP

A comment is something that is ignored and not read or executed by the PHP engine; it is written to make the code more readable and understandable. Comments are used to help other users and developers describe the code and what it is trying to do, and can also be used to document a set of code or part of a program.
PHP supports two types of comment:
Case Sensitivity in PHP
1. PHP is insensitive to whitespace

This includes all types of spaces that are invisible on the screen, including tabs, spaces and carriage returns. Even one space is equal to any number of spaces or carriage returns — PHP ignores all the spaces or tabs in a single row and carriage returns in multiple rows. Unless a semi-colon is encountered, PHP treats multiple lines as a single command.

<?php
// PHP code illustrate the whitespace insensitivity
$var1 = 15;
$var2 = 30;
$sum  = $var1+ $var2;
// "\n" for new line
echo $sum, "\n";
$sum1 = $var1  +   $var2;
echo $sum1;
?>

// Output — here both of them show the same results without any errors.
2. PHP is case-sensitive — but only for variables
All the keywords, functions and class names in PHP (while, if, echo etc.) are NOT case-sensitive, except variables. Only variables with different cases are treated differently.

<?php
// Here we can see that all echo
// statements are executed in the same manner
$variable = 25;
echo $variable;
ECHO $variable;
EcHo $variable;
// but this line will show RUNTIME ERROR as
// "Undefined Variable"
echo $VARIABLE;
?>
Blocks in PHP
In PHP, multiple statements can be executed simultaneously (under a single condition or loop) by using curly braces {}. This forms a block of statements that gets executed together.

<?php
$var = 50;
if ($var > 0){
   echo ("Positive as \n");
   echo ("greater than 0");
}
?>

// Output
Positive as
Greater than 0
PHP data types are used to hold different types of data or values. PHP supports 8 primitive data types, which can be categorised further into 3 types:

blocks.caption: The three categories of PHP data type
head: Category
Meaning
Data types

blocks.text: 1. Scalar Types
a. PHP Boolean

Booleans are the simplest data type and work like a switch. They hold only two values: TRUE (1) or FALSE (0). They are often used with conditional statements — if the condition is correct it returns TRUE, otherwise FALSE.

<?php
if (TRUE)
   echo "This condition is TRUE.";
if (FALSE)
   echo "This condition is FALSE.";
?>

// Output
This condition is TRUE.
b. PHP Integer
Integer means numeric data with a negative or positive sign. It holds only whole numbers — that is, numbers without a fractional part or decimal points.

blocks.title: Rules for integer:
items: An integer can be either positive or negative.
An integer must not contain a decimal point.
An integer can be decimal (base 10), octal (base 8) or hexadecimal (base 16).
The range of an integer must lie between -2,147,483,648 and 2,147,483,647, i.e. -2^31 to 2^31.

blocks.text:
<?php
$dec1  = 34;
$oct1  = 0243;
$hexa1 = 0x45;
echo "Decimal number 34 in decimal: " .$dec1. "</br>";
echo "Octal number: " .$oct1. "</br>";
echo "HexaDecimal number 0X45 in decimal: " .$hexa1. "</br>";
?>

// Output
Decimal number in decimal: 34
Octal number 0243 in decimal: 163
HexaDecimal number 0x45 in decimal: 69
c. PHP Float
A floating-point number is a number with a decimal point. Unlike an integer, it can hold numbers with a fractional or decimal point, including a negative or positive sign.

<?php
$n1  = 19.34;
$n2  = 54.472;
$sum = $n1 + $n2;
echo "Addition of floating numbers: " .$sum;
?>

// Output
Addition of floating numbers: 73.812
d. PHP String

A string is a non-numeric data type; it holds letters, alphabets, numbers and even special characters. String values must be enclosed either within single quotes or within double quotes — but the two are treated differently.

<?php
$company = "Javatpoint";
//both single and double quote statements will treat differently
echo "Hello $company";
echo "</br>";
echo 'Hello $company';
?>

// Output
Hello Javatpoint
Hello $company

blocks.title: Single vs double quotes
blocks.text: Inside double quotes a variable is expanded (interpolated): "Hello $company" prints Hello Javatpoint. Inside single quotes the text is printed literally: 'Hello $company' prints Hello $company. This is a favourite exam question.
2. Compound Types
a. PHP Array

An array is a data structure that stores one or more similar or dissimilar types of values in a single value. For example, if you want to store 100 numbers, instead of defining 100 variables it is easy to define an array of length 100.

<?php
$bikes = array (1001, "Yamaha", "KTM");
var_dump($bikes);   //the var_dump() function returns the datatype and values
echo "</br>";
echo "Array Element1: $bikes[0] </br>";
echo "Array Element2: $bikes[1] </br>";
echo "Array Element3: $bikes[2] </br>";
?>

// Output
array(3) { [0]=> int(1001) [1]=> string(6) "Yamaha" [2]=> string(3) "KTM" }
Array Element1: 1001
Array Element2: Yamaha
Array Element3: KTM
There are three different kinds of array, and each array value is accessed using an ID which is called the array index.

blocks.caption: Three kinds of PHP array
head: Kind
Description
rows: An array with a numeric index. Values are stored and accessed in linear fashion.
An array with strings as index. It stores element values in association with key values rather than in a strict linear index order.
An array containing one or more arrays; values are accessed using multiple indices.

blocks.text: Associative arrays are very similar to numeric arrays in functionality but different in their index: the index is a string, so you can establish a strong association between keys and values. To store the salaries of employees, a numerically indexed array would not be the best choice — instead you use the employees' names as the keys and their salaries as the values. There are two ways to define an associative array:

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: The associative array is used in PHP form handling and database connectivity — it is exactly how $_POST['name'] and a fetched database row are structured.
b. PHP Object
Objects are instances of user-defined classes that can store both values and functions. They must be explicitly declared.

<?php
class bike {
   function model() {
      $model_name = "Royal Enfield";
      echo "Bike Model: " .$model_name;
   }
}
$obj = new bike();
$obj -> model();
?>

// Output
Bike Model: Royal Enfield
3. Special Types

items: PHP Resource: resources are not an exact data type in PHP. They are used to store some function calls or references to external PHP resources — for example a database call, which is an external resource.

PHP Null: Null is a special data type that has only one value, NULL. There is a convention of writing it in capital letters, as it is case-sensitive. The special data type NULL defines a variable with no value.

blocks.text:
<?php
$nl = NULL;
echo $nl;   //it will not give any output
?>

blocks.text: Precedence of PHP Operators

Operator precedence determines the grouping of terms in an expression, which affects how the expression is evaluated. Certain operators have higher precedence than others; for example, the multiplication operator has higher precedence than the addition operator. In x = 7 + 3 * 2; x is assigned 13, not 20, because * has higher precedence than +.
Operators with the highest precedence appear at the top of the table and those with the lowest at the bottom. Within an expression, higher-precedence operators are evaluated first.

blocks.text: Sometimes it is convenient to be able to have variable variable names — that is, a variable name which can be set and used dynamically. A normal variable is set with a statement such as:

<?php
   $a = 'hello';
?>
A variable variable takes the value of a variable and treats that as the name of a variable. In the example above, hello can be used as the name of a variable by using two dollar signs:

<?php
   $$a = 'world';
?>
At this point two variables have been defined and stored in the PHP symbol tree: $a with the contents "hello" and $hello with the contents "world". Therefore this statement:

<?php
   echo "$a ${$a}";
?>

// produces exactly the same output as:

<?php
   echo "$a $hello";
?>

// i.e. they both produce:
hello world

To use variable variables with arrays you have to resolve an ambiguity problem: if you write $$a[1] the parser needs to know whether you meant to use $a[1] as a variable, or whether you wanted $$a as the variable and then the [1] index from that variable. The syntax for resolving this ambiguity is ${$a[1]} for the first case and ${$a}[1] for the second.

Class properties may also be accessed using variable property names. The variable property name is resolved within the scope from which the call is made — for instance, in the expression $foo->$bar the local scope is examined for $bar, and its value is used as the name of the property of $foo. This is also true if $bar is an array access. Curly braces may also be used to clearly delimit the property name; they are most useful when accessing values within a property that contains an array, when the property name is made up of multiple parts, or when the property name contains characters that are not otherwise valid (for example from json_decode() or SimpleXML).
PHP Super Global Variables

Some predefined variables in PHP are "superglobals", which means they are always accessible regardless of scope — you can access them from any function, class or file without having to do anything special. The PHP superglobal variables are:

items: $GLOBALS — used to access global variables from anywhere in the PHP script, including from within functions or methods.
$_SERVER — holds information about headers, paths and script locations.
$_REQUEST — used to collect data after submitting an HTML form.
$_POST — used to collect form data after submitting an HTML form with method="post". It is also widely used to pass variables.
$_GET — used to collect form data after submitting an HTML form with method="get".

blocks.text: Some other superglobal variables are $_FILES, $_ENV, $_COOKIE and $_SESSION.
PHP Form Handling

We can create and use forms in PHP. To get form data we need to use the PHP superglobals $_GET and $_POST. The form request may be get or post: to retrieve data from a GET request we use $_GET, and for a POST request we use $_POST.
The GET Method

items: The GET method sends the encoded user information appended to the page request; the page and the encoded information are separated by the ? character.
Example: http://www.test.com/index.htm?name1=value1&name2=value2
The GET method produces a long string that appears in your server logs and in the browser's Location box.
The GET method is restricted to sending up to 1024 characters only.
Never use the GET method if you have a password or other sensitive information to send to the server.
GET cannot be used to send binary data, such as images or Word documents, to the server.
The data sent by the GET method can be accessed using the QUERY_STRING environment variable.
PHP provides the $_GET associative array to access all the information sent using the GET method.

blocks.text: The POST Method

items: The POST method transfers information via HTTP headers. The information is encoded as described for the GET method and put into a header called QUERY_STRING.
The POST method does not have any restriction on the data size to be sent.
The POST method can be used to send ASCII as well as binary data.
The data sent by the POST method goes through the HTTP header, so security depends on the HTTP protocol; by using Secure HTTP you can make sure that your information is secure.
PHP provides the $_POST associative array to access all the information sent using the POST method.
